subject: Different output using different data stack

messages.author: ff2a321e956a7e2a
messages.subject: Different output using different data stack
parts:
Hi all

I'm trying to fit a spatial model using SPDE. I'm using the formula

resp~0+beta0+f(f1,model='rw1')+f(f2,model='iid')+f(s,model=spde)

'resp' is a beta variable, f1 is a continuous variable and f2 is a factor with 4 levels.

In spite of fitting the same model, INLA output was different for estimation only and for estimation+prediction. Is that possible or am I doing something wrong?

    Thanks

Marcial Marín

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different output using different data stack
parts:
On 23/09/14 11:47, M M wrote:
> Hi all
>
> I'm trying to fit a spatial model using SPDE. I'm using the formula
>
> resp~0+beta0+f(f1,model='rw1')+f(f2,model='iid')+f(s,model=spde)
>
> 'resp' is a beta variable, f1 is a continuous variable and f2 is a
> factor with 4 levels.
>
> In spite of fitting the same model, INLA output was different for
> estimation only and for estimation+prediction. Is that possible or am I
> doing something wrong?

This is possible, due to how the numerics is implemented internally.
Usually, the difference is within numerical tolerance, but for large
models with hard to identify parameters, the optimisation may terminate
at a different place when the prediction part is included.
Which category your model falls into depends on how much and in what way
your results differ.

A more stable, and generally faster, approach is to make two inla()
calls, where only the second includes the prediction, is started at the
precious parameter estimate (and restart=FALSE to prevent further
optimsation). I believe there is a FAQ entry on this.

Finn

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different output using different data stack
parts:
On 23/09/14 16:48, Marcial Marín wrote:
> Hi again
>
> I tried to make two inla() calls, including in the second one the
> prediction stack and including the control.mode argument
>
>
> control.mode=list(result=res5,restart=FALSE)
>
> Inla crashes and returns an error message
>
> *** ERROR *** N = 5437 but nx_file = 2656. Stop.
>
> Please could anyone give some idea of what is happening?

Since the two calls don't have the same model size you need to
specifically extract the estimated theta-vector instead of using the
whole "res5" structure. The documentation has this:

control.mode=list(theta=res5$mode$theta,restart=FALSE)

(In some old code I have res5$misc$theta.mode instead; I haven't tested
which method is actually correct in the current package version.)

Finn

messages.author: ff2a321e956a7e2a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different output using different data stack
parts:
Hi Finn, thank for your suggestion

     Yes, they overlap almost perfectly. I think it was a problem with workspace.

     I was fitting some models with different covariables. I've had some warnings about the Hessian for some models, so I used control.inla to adjust the Hessian and run several times those models with different values for the diagonal. Once estimated all the models I compared DICs and I selected the better one. I used that model to compare with the extended stack data, and the result led to my question. Nevertheless, 95% hpd intervals for hyperparameters fitted quite well.

     But I cleared my workspace and begin again. Today I fitted only the model selected yesterday. I found that, this time, I had no problems with Hessian. I fitted the extended model (with prediction) and I revised DIC, and hyperparameters. They fit much better than yesterday, there was a difference of about 2 units on DIC and up to  4% on hyperparameters mean (yesterday up to 43%!). The 95% hpd intervals overlap much more than those of yesterday, and plotting the fitted values from prediction and estimation gives the same result.

    So I think that something was wrong in the workspace, perhaps an object generated by R in the first few fitting processes and that was used later without changing his value. Could it be possible?

Marcial

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different output using different data stack
parts:
Hi,

I think you're running an old version, as this seems to work fine.

> r = inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=1:10),family="poisson")
> r = inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=1:10),family="poisson",
control.mode=list(theta=r$mode$theta, restart=FALSE))
> r = inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=1:10),family="poisson",
control.mode=list(result=r))


note that you can also just pass the 'result', which will also pass on
the mode for the latent field.

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Different output using different data stack
parts:
On 24/03/15 16:37, INLA help wrote:
> note that you can also just pass the 'result', which will also pass on
> the mode for the latent field.

No, the keyword here is "when doing prediction". The second inla call
doesn't have the same size of the linear predictor, so using result=r
will not work, and specifying only the theta-mode is the right approach.
r = inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=1:10),family="poisson")

r2 = inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=1:10),family="poisson",
control.mode=list(theta=r$mode$theta,restart=FALSE))
r3 = inla(y~1,data=data.frame(y=1:11),family="poisson",
control.mode=list(result=r,restart=FALSE))
*** ERROR *** N = 12 but nx_file = 11. Stop.

But yes, make sure that you have an updated INLA package installed,
and if it still doesn't work, please provide more details of _how_
it doesn't work. (Copies of error messages, warnings, etc)

Finn
